newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Direction mixed as buyers absent.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Direction mixed as buyers absent.

text.p: Direction was mixed for Singapore gas oil and jet fuel on Monday as sellers continued to dominate while buyers remained at bay, traders said.
"Sentiment has been contradictory with some players holding to the belief that the market is bullish while others thought that it remained bearish," one trader said.

The more optimistic traders pointed to potentially improved demand from China as the recent clampdown on smuggling in the southern provinces has helped to limit excess supplies and boosted prices to 2,100 from 1,800 yuan.
The high stocks on the mainland were due to a 93-percent jump in gas oil imports in the first half of this year to 4.2 million tonnes, compared with the same period last year.
This prompted China to try to curb imports in the second half and clamped down on smuggling which caused nervousness among the regional trading companies.

But those traders who held more bearish views said that despite anticipation of increased buying from China, no real buying flurry has been seen and only scattered sales were seen. For example, a Chinese trader last week sold a 30,000-tonne cargo of Okinawa gas oil from a Japanese refiner at $178 per
tonne, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) southern China.

Traders were also mixed about the volume of gas oil that India would take in its tender for September. They noted that state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) took only six to seven cargoes in September last year, which would leave a bearish note on the market.
Three sellers appeared for mid-to-second-half August liftings ranging between $22.60-$22.85 per barrel, free-on-board (fob) basis, almost unchanged from Friday's levels. Buyers remained sidelined.
Swaps gas oil was heard traded at $22.55 and $22.60 per barrel, but the players were not confirmed.
Sentiment was worse on jet fuel with swaps August regrade sliding to 40/60 cents per barrel from Friday's $0.85/$1.00. August regrade traded at 55 cents.
September also softened to $0.85/$1.00, from Friday's $1.10/$1.30.

Traders said even though the fourth quarter regrade was indicated at $1.90/$1.95, they said this could eventually slip to less than 80 cents. "Looking at the fourth quarter of 1996, the regrade never exceed $2.00," one trader said.
Traders said if the same mild winter seen last year were to repeat itself this year, the jet/kerosene fuel values would again be under pressure.
